messages.content:
A reader of a contract claims that the quoted passages below settle a statement (the hypothesis). You do not see the contract; judge only from the quotes.

<hypothesis>
Receiving Party shall not solicit some of Disclosing Party's representatives.
</hypothesis>

<claimed_label>
Entailment
</claimed_label>

<quotes>
<quote>each party agrees not to solicit or recruit any employee of each other without the prior written consent of that party</quote>
<quote>will not solicit for hire, in any capacity whatsoever, any of each other’s employees, contractors or other such affiliated resources</quote>
</quotes>

The labels mean:
- Entailment: the quotes state or clearly imply that the hypothesis is true.
- Contradiction: the quotes state or clearly imply that the hypothesis is false.

Decide whether the quotes, taken as written, are enough on their own to support the claimed label. Answer supports = false if the quotes are about something else, support the opposite label, support only part of the hypothesis, or need context the quotes do not give.

Answer only with the JSON object the response format asks for: supports (true or false) and a one-sentence reason.

content.text: {"supports":true,"reason":"The quotes bind each party not to solicit the other's employees, contractors or affiliated resources, so the Receiving Party may not solicit at least some of the Disclosing Party's representatives, which is what the hypothesis says."}
